question: A woodcutter earns ₹500 per day and spends 30% of his earning daily. What is his daily saving (in ₹)?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If the woodcutter spends 30%, he must be saving (100% − 30%) = 70%.

Daily saving = 70% of ₹500 = 0.7 × 500 = ₹350.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹350.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
• 
 
• 
 
• 
 Total Earnings = ₹500 (100%)
 
 Spent (30%)
 ₹150
 
 Saved (70%)
 ₹350

**Given:**

Daily earning of the woodcutter = ₹500

Percentage spent daily = 30%

**Formula Used:**

Savings = Total Earnings − Expenditure

**Calculations:**

⇒ Expenditure = 30% of ₹500

⇒ Expenditure = (30 ÷ 100) × 500 = ₹150

⇒ Savings = 500 − 150 = ₹350

**∴ The correct answer is ₹350.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Income and Expenditure relation

Total Income is always equal to the sum of Expenditure and Savings. Expressed as: Income = Expenditure + Savings.

Finding the Base Value

If the final value and the percentage of a part are given, the total base value can be found using: Base = (Part Value ÷ Percentage) × 100.

Successive Percentages

When spending occurs successively on remaining amounts, use the multiplying factor method: Final Amount = Initial Amount × (1 − p₁ ÷ 100) × (1 − p₂ ÷ 100).
